title: Why are so many students protesting in France?
description:
Across France, thousands of high school students are protesting. They say they’re doing it because of conditions in their schools - that classrooms are overcrowded, there’s not enough teachers and they can’t concentrate on exams because school buildings aren’t being maintained well enough.

Five hundred schools are shut and some protests have turned violent, with riot police being deployed and some streets set on fire. Pupils, teachers and police have been injured. Many of the protesters are under 18 and at this point there is no sign of the demonstrations ending. So why is this happening?

We hear from French teenagers who have spent the last few days protesting about what they want to change and why this is so important to them. We also hear from BBC reporter Pierre-Antoine Denis and former student union president Manès Nadel.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討法國高中生為何大規模抗議教育環境。學生反映教室過度擁擠、師資不足、校舍失修，以及不同地區資源分配不均；抗議從巴黎擴散到馬賽、里昂等城市。部分示威演變成衝突並造成傷者，政府指控政治活動人士混入學生運動煽動暴力，也有學生否認參與破壞，並有人質疑警方對和平示威者的處理方式。政府表示將改善設施、維持上課與提高大學入學程序的透明度，但抗議組織認為缺乏具體措施。節目也分析總統大選將近的時機，說明許多尚未取得投票資格的學生，希望藉由示威讓候選人重視教育與他們的未來。
summaryEn: This episode examines why high school students across France are protesting. Students describe overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, deteriorating buildings, and unequal resources. Demonstrations spread from Paris to cities including Marseille and Lyon. Some turned violent and caused injuries. Authorities allege that political activists infiltrated the movement, while some students deny responsibility for damage and others challenge the police response to peaceful protesters. The government says it will address school facilities, keep classes running, and make university admissions more transparent, but protest organizers say the measures are not concrete enough. With a presidential election approaching, the programme explains why students who are too young to vote are using demonstrations to press candidates to prioritize education and their future.
